Analysis. NHTSA used vehicle mortality figures in conducting the engineering analysis for the fuel economy standard. Also, a schedule of vehicle miles traveled was used which reflected an average yearly mileage greater than 15,000 miles per year in the first years of use falling to less than 7000 miles per year in the later years. This screenie has collapsed to an average miles traveled per year over the life of the vehicle and a lifetime in years that reflected the average lifetime total mileage. This averaging was done to simplify the analysis presented , in the EIS. THe source of the mileage information was the 1972 Census of Transportation, Truck Inventory and Use Survey, U. S. Department of Commerce, Bureau of the Census. NHTSA sees no reason to change the assumptions or the analysis, in light of the much greater uncertainty in predicting manufacturer and consumer response to fuel economy standards.
